name: Arizona State University
description: In the heart of Tempe, ASU is a key factor in its vibrant, diverse and progressive lifestyle. It was founded as a Normal (Teaching) school in 1885. Arizona State is now one of the largest universities in the nation, with several campuses spread throughout the metropolitan area. The largest of these…

name: Old Main
description: The original school's building, dating back to its founding.

name: Gammage Memorial Auditorium
description: A theater designed by Frank Lloyd Wright that hosts international talent, Broadway shows, and local entertainment. One of his last architectural pieces, it was designed for Baghdad before being built in the equally arid Valley of the Sun.

name: ASU Mars Space Flight Facility
description: Supports the Thermal Emission Spectrometer experiment that was sent aboard the Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft when it launched in November 1996. The Mars facility has a visitor area with displays about Mars and a television tuned to NASA TV.

name: ASU Robert S. Dietz Museum of Geology
description: Houses minerals, gems, fossils from Arizona and around the world. It also has a six-story Foucault pendulum; local fossils including Colombian mammoth remains excavated in 1985, 1997 and 1999; real dinosaurs, a giant-extinct fossil shark over 7 ft (2.1 m) tall (featured on the National Geographic…

name: ASU Center for Meteorite Studies
description: Houses the world's largest university-based meteorite collection, with specimens from more than 1700 separate meteorite falls. Portions of this collection are on display to the public.

name: ASU Art Museum
description: Has a fine permanent collection and an active guest artist program. The attached gift shop is, surprisingly, a great place to get beautiful and unusual gifts.

name: Hayden Library
description: A vast collection housed mostly underground in the center of campus. It has many unique features, including the only Child Drama collection, various exhibits, and rare and valuable works available to the public through the Luhrs reading room. Where else can one walk in and request to see a page…

name: Life Sciences Tower
description: Has glass cases set into the hallways that house dozens of reptiles, including a comprehensive sampling of the poisonous snakes of Arizona.

name: ASU Museum of Anthropology
description: Run by the internationally acclaimed School of Human Evolution and Social Change, has many interesting permanent and visiting exhibits throughout the year.

name: Northlight Gallery
description: Exhibits a broad range of photographic work by emerging and international recognized artists.
hours: Tue 12:30-8:30PM, Wed-Sat 12:30-4:30PM; closed on major holidays and in summer

name: AZ Heritage Center at Papago Park
description: A museum that concentrates on Arizona's history in the 20th and 21st centuries.

name: Tempe History Museum
description: Features the history of Tempe from the time of prehistoric Hohokam to today. Video, hands-on exhibits and gift shop.

name: City of Tempe Cultural Services Public Art
description: Numerous examples of public art dot Tempe's landscape. Additionally, Tempe presents exhibits featuring professional and student artists. Works may be viewed in public places, which serve as alternate spaces for regularly changing exhibits.

name: Petersen House Museum
description: Restored Queen Anne Victorian home built in 1892 by one of Tempe's earliest settlers.

name: Tempe Center for the Arts
description: For events see the event calendar .

name: Salt River Project History Center
description: Has exhibits illustrating the construction of the Theodore Roosevelt Dam, as well as other exhibits relating to the history of water usage in Arizona.

name: Sea Life Arizona
description: Has a walk-through aquarium, and 30 displays.
price: $12 online/$18 at gate (adults 13+), $12 online/$13 at gate (children 3-12)

name: Tempe Town Lake
description: Set adjacent to Tempe's Mill Avenue District, Arizona State University and the 2,000 acres (810 hectares) Papago Park, Tempe Town Lake embodies a unique vision for the future of the Valley. It is the center for many activities like boating, biking etc and has a jogger's track as well. The sight of…

name: Ironman Arizona
description: Held annually in November.

name: P.F. Chang's Rock'n'Roll Arizona Marathon and Half Marathon
description: Held annually in January.

name: Buffalo Wild Wings Bowl
description: Annually in December.

name: Angels Major League Baseball Spring Training
description: Hosted every March.

name: Tempe Festival of the Arts
description: Massive twice yearly street fair featuring arts and crafts from all over the country, as well as a wide selection of carnival/street fair style foods, beverages and live entertainment. Held at the end of March and beginning of December.

name: Cafe Lalibela
description: Cafe Lalibela is a family restaurant bringing Ethiopian cuisine to the heart of Tempe. Takeout available.
hours: Mon-Thu 11AM-9PM, Fri 11AM-10PM, Sat noon-10PM, Sun noon-9PM

name: Cornish Pasty Co
description: A British and Irish themed restaurant and bar offers a wide range of classic, modern, and experimental pasties with a number of European beers available on tap. It is popular with Tempe's younger and bohemian crowd.

name: Green New American Vegetarian
description: Vegan restaurant that was named the best vegan restaurant in Phoenix by the Phoenix New Times. PETA named the secret BBQ Chicken sandwich as the best faux chicken sandwich in the USA. Another location in Central Phoenix.

name: La Fonda Mexican Food
description: La Fonda is a great restaurant if you're looking for Mexican food. The food is excellent, and the atmosphere is friendly; good pricing is an added benefit, not a factor.

name: Little Szechwan
description: Family-run Chinese restaurant. Mouth-watering food and very friendly service.

name: Munch a Mania
description: The food is wonderful, portion sizes are great, and the service is the most personal you will get in town. Free delivery ($10 minimum order).

name: My Big Fat Greek Restaurant
description: Delivers large portions of Greek food and is a favorite of many ASU college students.

name: Phoenicia Cafe
description: Delicious Mediterranean and Middle Eastern food. Relatively small and often packed, esp. while the university nearby is in session. Try the babaganouj (eggplant dip) and the baklava, made from scratch. There is also an attached small Middle Eastern grocery that has great prices, especially on…

name: Rosita's Fine Mexican Food
description: This popular, long-established family restaurant serves up Mexican classic dishes with a focus on Sonoran cooking.

name: Courtyard Tempe Downtown
description: 10 minute free shuttle ride from your flight into Sky Harbor Airport. From there you are just blocks from downtown Tempe and Arizona State University.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Tempe
description: Rates include free wi-fi and breakfast. 12 mi (19 km) from downtown Phoenix.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Phoenix Tempe - University
description: Located within walking distance of ASU, this hotel offers proximity to local area attractions in a room with various full-service accommodations. Includes breakfast and wi-fi.

name: Quality Inn Airport Tempe
description: Centrally located near the airport, ASU, the Mill Avenue District, and Tempe Town Lake. Pets accepted.

name: Quality Inn at ASU
description: This hotel is 5 mi (8.0 km) from the airport and very close to ASU. Easy access to freeways for travel in Tempe. Breakfast and wi-fi included.

name: Tempe Mission Palms Hotel
description: Upscale 303-room hotel with courtyard and roof top pool, 30,000 ft² (2,800 m 2 ) of conference space, 10 ADA rooms, restaurant. AAA/CAA & TAG approved.
